messages.subject: R ctmm errors
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am new to ctmm and still beginner in r.
I try to derive homeranges from animal tracking data using the aKDE (ctmm) approach.
I applied the same workflow as used in the provided example in the ctmm.pdf manual. It does work for some of my data, but it doesn't for others.

I receive the following error message in R-Studio:

3: stats::optim(par = par, fn = fn, method = method, lower = lower,
       upper = upper, control = control, ...)
2: Optimizer(par = pars, fn = fn, method = optimizer, lower = lower,
       upper = upper, period = period, control = control)
1: ctmm.fit(track_h, GUESS)

regards
stefan

PS:
here is the dataset I used: link <https://www.dropbox.com/s/s90gj7f9kvilnc4/animalTracks.csv?dl=0>
this is the code I used:

tracks <- as.telemetry('animalTracks.csv',timeformat="",timezone="UTC",projection=NULL,timeout=Inf,na.rm="row",drop=TRUE)

trackIDs <- names(tracks)
no_tracks <- length(trackIDs)

for(i in 1:no_tracks ){ #no_tracks) {
  track_i <- tracks[i]
  names(track_i) <- "1"
  track_h <- track_i$'1'
  GUESS <- ctmm.guess(track_h,interactive=FALSE)
  print(i)
  FIT <- ctmm.fit(track_h,GUESS)
  UD <- akde(track_h,FIT)

  assign(paste("UD", i, sep = ""), UD)

}

messages.subject: Re: R ctmm errors
messages.body_plain:
Hi Stefan,

This CSV is interpreted as belonging to one individual because there is no MoveBank-style identity column. I do not know if that is intended or not, but as.telemetry() produces some warnings related to that.
Therefore, when you start indexing the telemetry object tracks, I do not think you are feeding a proper telemetry object into the later functions but probably just some columns of the telemetry object.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Looping/automating home range estimation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

In my use of ctmm to create AKDE home range estimates so far, I have been running through the code for each individual at a time to determine parameters for each animal's model. I'm wondering if it is possible to automate the process using a for loop or any other way. I am hoping to estimate seasonal home ranges for 20+ individuals, so that would be ~80 models that I'm hoping to run.

Thanks much,
Dave

messages.subject: Re: Looping/automating home range estimation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dave,

In a loop you can use interactive=FALSE of ctmm.guess(). I would also output/save a comparison plot of the empirical & model variograms, to check over afterwards.

https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/reference/variogram.fit.html

Mike automated everything for 369 individuals in the recent Ecological Monographs paper: https://esajournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ecm.1344
I believe he provided code in one of the appendices.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Interpolation between locations?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

Pardon this very basic question - but does AKDE interpolate use between locations in the sense that BBMM or BRB does?

I understand the estimator incorporates time between points, but I also see that it functions as a KDE would when samples are separated by enough time that autocorrelation reduces greatly.

The reason that I ask is that I have GPS data for a very mobile species (bobcats) that has variable intervals due to very low fix success. Some points are separated by as little as 1 hour, while other points are separated by several days. As a result, the steps with very long time lags need to be discarded from these aforementioned movement modeling approaches to avoid overestimation. The problem is that these data with long time lags make up a large chunk of the data for some individuals, and I am losing a lot of information by discarding them. So, I have chunks of highly correlated points interspersed with less correlated points.

My current understanding is that I may need to either discard the less autocorrelated data to fit a movement model, or downgrade to an estimator that assumes independence such as standard KDE or LoCoH. I would greatly appreciate any insight you have on this.

Thanks much,
Dave

messages.subject: Re: Interpolation between locations?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dave,

Sampling irregularity can be accounted for in AKDE by optimally weighting the data (the weights option in akde()):
https://esajournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/eap.1704
https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/reference/bandwidth.html

When I first derived AKDE, I also derived a separate estimator that filled in the gaps (a hybrid between AKDE and the Kriged occurrence distribution), so it is possible. However, when gaps are short, then the optimal bandwidth is much larger than the gaps, making this fruitless. On the other hand, when there are large gaps, then by filling them in you get a over-smoothed estimate and give up asymptotic consistency. Optimal weights fixes the same problem in a much better way.

Best,
Chris
